ACCEPT.doc: Wait for and accept a single keystroke/character from the channel without echo or requiring Enter, storing it in the variable(s).

ADD.doc: ADD directive taking a string argument (e.g. adding a name to a list/library). Semantics not confirmed.

ADDR.doc: Add a program to resident memory so subsequent CALL/PERFORM/RUN of it do not reload it from disk. Use DROP to remove it.

AND.doc: Logical AND operator: true (1) when both operands are non-zero. Used in IF, WHILE, UNTIL and other conditions.

AUTO.doc: Command-mode directive: turn on automatic line numbering for entering program statements.

AUTO_LOCK.doc: Turn automatic record locking on or off.

BEGIN.doc: Close all open files (except channel 0) and reset the program state. Also used as a clause in SELECT ... BEGIN key$ to give the starting key of the selection.

BREAK.doc: Exit the innermost FOR/NEXT, WHILE/WEND, REPEAT/UNTIL or SELECT/NEXT RECORD loop and continue after its end.

BUTTON.doc: Create, delete or manipulate a push-button GUI control. Pressing the button generates the CTL value ctl_id.

CALL.doc: Call an external program (or entry point label via "prog;label") as a subroutine, passing arguments by reference. The called program receives them with ENTER and returns with EXIT.

CASE.doc: Introduces a branch inside SWITCH ... END SWITCH; executed when the SWITCH expression matches one of the values.

CATCH.doc: Starts the error-handling section of a TRY ... CATCH ... END_TRY block; executed when an error occurs in the TRY section.

CHART.doc: Create, remove or manipulate a chart (graph) GUI control.

CHECK_BOX.doc: Create, read, write or manipulate a check box GUI control.

syntax: DEF CLASS "name"[ CREATE REQUIRED][ DELETE REQUIRED]
CLASS.doc: Keyword of DEF CLASS used to define an object class in an OOP program.

CLEAR.doc: Clear (reset) variables: with no list all local variables are cleared; with a list only those variables are reset to 0/null.

CLIP_BOARD.doc: Read from or write to the Windows clipboard.

CLOSE.doc: Close one or more channels (files/devices). CLOSE with no channel closes all channels opened by the program (except 0).

CONTINUE.doc: Skip the rest of the current loop iteration and continue with the next iteration of the innermost loop.

CONTROL.doc: Keyword used after ENABLE/DISABLE/HIDE/SHOW etc. to refer to a GUI control.

CREATE.doc: Keyword: in DEF CLASS, CREATE REQUIRED requires the class to define an ON_CREATE constructor. Also a directive taking two strings (semantics not confirmed).

CUSTOM_VBX.doc: Create or remove a custom (VBX/OCX-style) GUI control. Only the REMOVE form was confirmed by the 9.62 checker.

CWDIR.doc: Change the current working directory (see LWD for the current directory).

DATA.doc: Define constants to be read with READ DATA; use RESTORE to reposition the data pointer.

DAY_FORMAT.doc: Set the date format used by the DAY system variable (e.g. "MM/DD/YY").

DEF.doc: Define a user function (DEF FN, single- or multi-line ending with END DEF), a class (DEF CLASS), or a COM/ActiveX object (DEF OBJECT).

DEFAULT.doc: Introduces the branch inside SWITCH ... END SWITCH executed when no CASE matches.

DEFCTL.doc: Define control-key (CTL) assignments. Syntax not confirmed by the 9.62 checker.

DEFPRT.doc: Define printer characteristics. Takes numeric arguments; semantics not confirmed.

DEFTTY.doc: Define terminal characteristics. Takes numeric arguments; semantics not confirmed.

DELETE.doc: Delete program lines (command mode). DELETE OBJECT destroys an object instance created with NEW().

DICTIONARY.doc: Keyword used with embedded data dictionary operations (e.g. reading/writing a file's dictionary).

DIM.doc: Dimension arrays with square brackets (numeric or string, up to 3 dimensions, e.g. DIM A$[10]) or, with parentheses, initialise a string variable to the given length (filled with spaces or fill$).

DIRECT.doc: Create a DIRECT (single-keyed, hashed) data file.

DISABLE.doc: Disable (grey out) a GUI control or object so it cannot be used.

DROP.doc: Remove a resident program (added by ADDR) from memory, or drop an object reference.

DROP_BOX.doc: Create or manipulate a drop-down list box GUI control.

DUMP.doc: List all variables and their current values (to the terminal or the given channel); useful for debugging.

EDIT.doc: Command-mode directive: edit a program statement. ` (backquote) is an alias.

syntax: IF cond THEN stmts ELSE stmts
ELSE.doc: Introduces the statements of an IF that execute when the condition is false.

ENABLE.doc: Enable a GUI control or object previously disabled.

END.doc: End program execution (closing files opened by the program). Also closes block structures: END DEF, END SWITCH; as a SELECT clause, END key$ gives the ending key.

END SWITCH.doc: Terminates a SWITCH ... CASE ... END SWITCH block.

ENDDEF.doc: Ends a multi-line DEF FN user function or a DEF CLASS definition.

ENDTRACE.doc: Stop program statement tracing started with SETTRACE.

syntax: IF cond THEN stmts [ELSE stmts] END_IF; stmt...
END_IF.doc: Terminates the THEN/ELSE scope of an IF on the same line, so the statements that follow END_IF execute regardless of the condition. FI is an alias.

END_TRY.doc: Terminates a TRY ... CATCH ... END_TRY structure.

ENTER.doc: Receive the arguments passed by CALL (by position) into local variables of the called program. Variables not listed are local.

ERASE.doc: Delete (erase) a file or empty directory from disk.

ERROR_HANDLER.doc: Define a program to be performed when an untrapped error occurs (null string clears it).

ESCAPE.doc: Interrupt program execution as if Escape/Break was pressed, entering command mode (debug).

EVENT.doc: Keyword used in event-related clauses (EVENT alone does not compile).

EXCEPT.doc: Clause/keyword used to exclude items (e.g. in variable lists or SELECT).

EXECUTE.doc: Compile and execute a statement held in a string expression.

EXIT.doc: Return from a CALLed program to the caller; with an error number, the error is raised in the calling program.

EXITTO.doc: Exit the current loop or subroutine and transfer control to the given statement/label (pops the loop/GOSUB stack).

EXTRACT.doc: Read a record and lock it for update; the file pointer is not advanced, so a following WRITE updates the same record.

FILE.doc: Create a file from a file description string.

FINALLY.doc: Introduces the section of TRY ... END_TRY that executes whether or not an error occurred (compiles in 9.62).

FIND.doc: Read a record by key/index without advancing the file pointer if not found; with DOM=/ERR= used to test existence.

FLOATINGPOINT.doc: Switch numeric arithmetic to floating-point mode (instead of fixed PRECISION decimal mode).

FOR.doc: Start a counted loop ending with NEXT [var]. FOR (chan) iterates over the records of a file.

FROM.doc: Clause of SELECT naming the channel or file to read.

FUNCTION.doc: Declare a method of a class inside DEF CLASS; the body starts at the given label (or the same-named label) and ends with RETURN value. FUNCTION LOCAL methods are private to the class.

GET.doc: Clause of PROPERTY naming the label that computes the value when the property is read.

GET_FILE_BOX.doc: Display the standard Windows open (or save, with WRITE) file dialog and return the selected path.

GOSUB.doc: Call a subroutine at the line number or label; RETURN resumes after the GOSUB.

GOTO.doc: Transfer control to the given line number or label.

GRID.doc: Create or manipulate a grid (spreadsheet-style) GUI control.

HIDE.doc: Hide a GUI control or window.

H_SCROLLBAR.doc: Create or manipulate a horizontal scroll bar GUI control.

syntax: IF cond THEN stmt[; stmt...] [ELSE stmt[; stmt...]] [END_IF]
IF.doc: Conditionally execute statements. In the single-line form the THEN (and ELSE) part runs to the end of the line, or up to END_IF, after which statements on the same line execute unconditionally. Use braces { } to span several lines.

INDEX.doc: Keyword used for index specifications (e.g. in key definitions).

INDEXED.doc: Create an INDEXED (fixed-length, record-number accessed) data file.

INPUT.doc: Read data from the terminal or a file into variables. On a terminal, a prompt and position may precede each variable; options like LEN=, TIM=, HLP= apply.

INSERT.doc: INSERT keyword (the 9.62 checker accepts any argument text, as for command-mode directives).

INVOKE.doc: Launch a Windows application/document (via the shell) from the program; INVOKE WAIT waits for it to end.

IOLIST.doc: Define a reusable list of variables referenced by IOL= options and the IOL() function.

KEY.doc: Keyword/option: the key value for keyed file access.

KEYED.doc: Create a KEYED (multi-keyed, variable-length capable) data file, optionally with multiple key definitions.

LET.doc: Assign values to variables. The LET keyword is optional.

LIKE.doc: Inside DEF CLASS, declares the class(es) this class inherits from.

LINE_SWITCH.doc: LINE_SWITCH directive (optional argument). Semantics not confirmed.

LIST.doc: Command-mode directive: list program statements to the terminal or a channel. \ is an alias.

LIST_BOX.doc: Create or manipulate a list box GUI control (including report-view list boxes).

LOAD.doc: Load a program into memory (command mode) for editing or running.

LOCAL.doc: Declare variables local to the current routine/method; FUNCTION LOCAL declares a private method in DEF CLASS.

LOCK.doc: Lock a file for exclusive use by this task (other users get Error #0 busy).

LONG_FORM.doc: Display/list program keywords in long (full) form.

MENU_BAR.doc: Create a menu bar on the window from a menu definition string.

MERGE.doc: Merge program statements read from a text file channel into the program in memory.

MESSAGE_LIB.doc: Set the message library used by MSG() and error messages.

MNEMONIC.doc: Define or redefine a mnemonic for a channel (the output sequence produced for 'XX').

MSGBOX.doc: Display a Windows message box; options select icon and buttons, and the button pressed is returned in var$.

MULTI_LINE.doc: Create or manipulate a multi-line (or single-line) text edit GUI control.

MULTI_MEDIA.doc: Play multimedia (sound/video) or send a command to a multimedia device.

NEXT.doc: End of a FOR loop: increment the loop variable and repeat if not past the end. NEXT RECORD ends a SELECT loop.

NEXT RECORD.doc: Ends a SELECT ... FROM ... NEXT RECORD loop.

OBJECT.doc: Keyword used with object directives (DELETE OBJECT, DROP OBJECT, DEF OBJECT).

OBTAIN.doc: Read keyboard input like INPUT but without echoing/displaying the characters.

OFF.doc: Keyword used to turn options off (e.g. 'CURSOR'("OFF"), PRECISION OFF style forms).

ON.doc: Computed branch: transfers to the reference selected by the (0-based) value of expr; values beyond the list go to the last reference.

OPEN.doc: Open a file or device on a channel. OPEN LOCK opens exclusively, OPEN INPUT opens read-only. Use UNT/HFN to obtain a free channel number.

OR.doc: Logical OR operator: true (1) when either operand is non-zero.

PASSWORD.doc: Assign a password to a data file.

PERFORM.doc: Call an external program that shares the caller's variables (no ENTER needed); control returns to the caller on EXIT.

POP.doc: Remove the most recent GOSUB return address / loop entry from the stack without returning.

PRECISION.doc: Set the number of decimal places to which numeric results are rounded (default 2).

PREFIX.doc: Set the search path (prefix list) used to locate files and programs; see PFX.

PREINPUT.doc: Supply characters (keystrokes) to be read by subsequent INPUTs as if typed.

PRINT.doc: Output data to the terminal or to a channel. Items may include mnemonics ('CS'), positioning @(col,line), and formatted numbers (n:mask$). ? is an alias.

PROCEED.doc: Keyword used as the *PROCEED branch target (PROCEED alone does not compile).

PROCESS.doc: Run an NOMADS panel (screen) definition from a library.

PROGRAM.doc: Create a program file; also a keyword in FUNCTION ... FOR PROGRAM and PREFIX PROGRAM.

PROPERTIES.doc: Keyword used with object/control properties (PROPERTIES alone does not compile).

syntax: PROPERTY name[$][ GET label][ SET label|ERR]
PROPERTY.doc: Declare a property of a class inside DEF CLASS, optionally with GET/SET labels for computed access (SET ERR makes it read-only). (PROPERTY LOCAL/HIDE do not compile in 9.62.)

PURGE.doc: Remove all records from an open file (empty it).

QUIT.doc: Terminate ProvideX and return to the operating system. BYE is an alias.

RADIO_BUTTON.doc: Create or manipulate a radio (option) button GUI control. Syntax not confirmed by the 9.62 checker.

RANDOMIZE.doc: Re-seed the random number generator used by RND with the given value (RANDOMIZE without an argument does not compile).

READ.doc: Read the next (or specified) record from a file into the variables. READ RECORD reads the whole record into one string; READ DATA reads DATA constants.

READDATA.doc: Read values from DATA statements (internal form of READ DATA).

RECORD.doc: Keyword modifying READ/WRITE/EXTRACT/FIND/INPUT: transfer the entire record as a single string without field parsing.

REDIM.doc: Re-dimension an existing array (square brackets), preserving existing elements where possible.

RELEASE.doc: Terminate ProvideX (release the session), like QUIT.

REM.doc: Remark (comment) statement; the rest of the line is ignored. ! also starts a comment.

REMOVE.doc: Delete the record with the given key (or index) from a file; DOM= traps a missing key.

RENUMBER.doc: Command-mode directive: renumber the program statements.

REPEAT.doc: Start a loop that executes at least once and repeats until the UNTIL condition is true.

REQUIRED.doc: Clause of DEF CLASS requiring the class to define ON_CREATE / ON_DELETE methods (constructor/destructor).

RESET.doc: Reset program state (stacks, error handling) and return to the start / command level.

RESTORE.doc: Reset the DATA pointer so that the next READ DATA reads from the beginning (or the given statement).

RETRY.doc: Re-execute the statement that caused the last error (used in error-handling routines).

RETURN.doc: Return from a GOSUB subroutine; in a DEF FN or object method, RETURN value returns the function result.

ROUND.doc: Turn numeric rounding (to PRECISION) on or off.

RUN.doc: Run the program in memory, or load and run the named program (all variables are cleared).

SAME.doc: Keyword referring to the same statement/value (e.g. as a branch target or option value).

SAVE.doc: Save the program in memory to disk (command mode).

SECURITY_MASK.doc: Read the security (permission) mask used when creating files.

syntax:
SELECT varlist FROM chan|file$ [BEGIN k$][END k$][KNO=n][WHERE cond]
  ...
NEXT RECORD
SELECT.doc: Loop over the records of a file (optionally limited by BEGIN/END keys and a WHERE condition), reading each into the variables; the loop ends with NEXT RECORD.

SERVER.doc: Keyword used with client/server (e.g. file server) operations.

SET.doc: Clause of PROPERTY naming the label executed when the property is assigned (SET ERR makes it read-only).

SETCTL.doc: Set control-key handling. Syntax not confirmed by the 9.62 checker.

SETDAY.doc: Set the date returned by the DAY system variable.

SETDEV.doc: Set device characteristics for a channel from a definition string.

SETERR.doc: Set a program-wide error branch: untrapped errors transfer to the statement; SETERR 0 cancels it.

SETESC.doc: Set an escape (interrupt) branch: pressing Escape/Break transfers to the statement; SETESC 0 cancels it.

SETFID.doc: Set the file/terminal identifier returned by FID().

SETMOUSE.doc: Turn mouse support on or off.

SETTIME.doc: Set the time returned by the TIM system variable.

SETTRACE.doc: Start tracing executed program statements (to the terminal or a channel); stop with ENDTRACE.

SET_FOCUS.doc: Move the input focus to the given GUI control.

SET_NBF.doc: SET_NBF directive taking a number or ON/OFF. Semantics not confirmed.

SET_PARAM.doc: Set (or with -'XX' clear) system parameters, e.g. SET_PARAM 'BY'=1900. Read them back with PRM('XX').

SHORT_FORM.doc: Display/list program keywords in their short (abbreviated) form.

SHOW.doc: Make a hidden GUI control/window visible.

START.doc: Restart ProvideX (clears everything and re-runs the start-up program). Do not use from embedded/COM sessions.

STATIC.doc: Declare static variables (the 9.62 checker accepts almost any argument text after STATIC).

syntax: FOR var=start TO end STEP inc
STEP.doc: Clause of FOR giving the increment (may be negative).

STOP.doc: Halt program execution and enter command mode (files remain open).

SWAP.doc: SWAP directive taking a parenthesised value (e.g. a window/channel number). Semantics not confirmed; SWAP a,b does not compile.

syntax:
SWITCH expr
  CASE v1[,v2]
    ...
  DEFAULT
    ...
END SWITCH
SWITCH.doc: Multi-way branch: compares expr against each CASE value and executes the matching branch (BREAK leaves the switch).

SYSTEM_HELP.doc: Invoke the Windows help system for the given help file/topic.

SYSTEM_JRNL.doc: Control the system journal (file update journaling); SYSTEM_JRNL CLOSE closes it.

TABLE.doc: Define a character translation table (hex byte list) referenced by TBL= options; the TABLE statement must be referenced by line number/label.

THEN.doc: Clause of IF introducing the statements executed when the condition is true.

TO.doc: Clause giving the end value of a FOR loop (also RENAME old$ TO new$).

TRANSLATE.doc: Set up character translation (from$ characters translated to to$).

TRISTATE_BOX.doc: Create or manipulate a three-state check box GUI control.

TRY.doc: Start a structured error-handling block: errors in the TRY section transfer to CATCH.

UNIQUE.doc: Keyword in key definitions marking a key as unique (no duplicates).

UNLOCK.doc: Release a file lock set by LOCK (or record locks held on the channel).

UNTIL.doc: End of a REPEAT loop: the loop repeats until the condition is true.

UPDATE.doc: UPDATE keyword (the 9.62 checker accepts any argument text, as for command-mode directives).

USER_LEX.doc: Define user lexical (keyword) extensions. Syntax not confirmed by the 9.62 checker.

VARDROP_BOX.doc: Create or manipulate a variable (editable) drop box GUI control.

VARLIST_BOX.doc: Create or manipulate a variable (editable) list box GUI control.

VIA.doc: Keyword used to access something via an object or reference.

VIDEO_PALETTE.doc: Set (or READ) the colour palette used for text colours.

V_SCROLLBAR.doc: Create or manipulate a vertical scroll bar GUI control.

WAIT.doc: Suspend execution for the given number of seconds.

WHERE.doc: Clause of SELECT giving a condition records must satisfy to be processed.

WHILE.doc: Loop while the condition is true; the loop body ends with WEND.

WINPRT_SETUP.doc: Read or set the Windows printer setup (printer selection/settings) as a string.

WITH.doc: WITH directive taking a numeric value. Semantics not confirmed.

WRITE.doc: Write a record (fields separated by SEP) to a file; on keyed files DOM= traps duplicate keys. WRITE RECORD writes a string as the whole record.

syntax:
DEF CLASS "name"[ CREATE REQUIRED][ DELETE REQUIRED]
  LIKE "parent"
  PROPERTY ...
  FUNCTION ...
END DEF
DEF CLASS.doc: Define an object class: its properties, methods (FUNCTION) and inheritance (LIKE), terminated by END DEF.

END DEF.doc: Terminates a multi-line DEF FN function or a DEF CLASS definition.

syntax:
DEF FNname[$](param,...)
  ...
  RETURN value
END DEF
DEF FN.doc: Define a user function, called as FNname(...) (string functions end in $). Multi-line functions return their value with RETURN and end with END DEF.

FUNCTION LOCAL.doc: Declare a method that can only be called from within the class (and its derived classes).

syntax: PROPERTY name GET get_label SET set_label
PROPERTY GET/SET.doc: Computed property: reading it performs the GET label (which RETURNs the value), assigning performs the SET label (new value is in the property variable).

ON GOTO/ON GOSUB.doc: Computed branch: expr=0 selects the first reference, 1 the second, etc.; values beyond the list select the last.

syntax: IF cond THEN stmt1 ELSE stmt2 END_IF; stmt3
IF..THEN..ELSE..END_IF.doc: IF with an END_IF terminator: stmt3 runs whatever the condition. Multi-line IF blocks use braces { } (a line ending in \ is NOT a continuation: \ is an alias of LIST).

syntax:
SELECT IOL=iol FROM "file" BEGIN start$ END end$ WHERE cond
  ...
NEXT RECORD
SELECT..FROM..BEGIN..END..WHERE.doc: Record selection loop over a file with optional key range and filter condition.

REPEAT/UNTIL.doc: Post-tested loop (body executes at least once).

syntax:
SWITCH expr
  CASE 1,2
    ...
    BREAK
  DEFAULT
    ...
END SWITCH

DEF OBJECT.doc: Create a COM (ActiveX/OLE automation) object, optionally as a visible control at the given position; the handle is used with handle'property and DELETE OBJECT.
